desc: Implement a helper function to compute combinations $\binom{n}{k} \pmod{10^9+7}$ efficiently using precomputed factorials and inverse factorials, handling the case where $k < 0$ or $k > n$.

Write a function to compute the sum of absolute differences for all pairs in a list of coordinates. For the grid, the x-coordinates consist of $n$ copies of each value from $0$ to $m-1$, and y-coordinates consist of $m$ copies of each value from $0$ to $n-1$.
Calculate the sum of x-distances: sort the x-coordinate list (or use the formula for sum of differences in a sorted array with multiplicities) and compute $\sum_{i<j} |x_i - x_j|$.
Calculate the sum of y-distances similarly using the y-coordinate list.
Compute the total sum of Manhattan distances over all pairs of cells as $(\text{sum\_x} + \text{sum\_y}) \pmod{10^9+7}$.
Multiply the total pair distance sum by $\binom{N-2}{k-2} \pmod{10^9+7}$ where $N = m \times n$, and return the result.
